@ a receiver in .up~(2).down~(2) sees at a tick the events before the frame of the tick: the events of the frames c and c + 1 come at the tick c + 2, and the run j has sample_tick() c + j
@ the same with the ratios 4 and 2, 2 and 4, and 4 2 2: every run of a tick sees the same events, and sample_tick() is 4 floor(c / 2) + j, 2 floor(c / 4) + j, c + j
@ a maker in .up~(2).down~(2) gives its two events at the frame of the tick, not at the frame of each run
@ a maker whose event is of the stage sample / 2 of its body gives an event for each run whose sample_tick() is even: one at each tick of .up~(2).down~(2), two of .up~(4).down~(2)
@ a reset by an event at the frame 3, between the ticks 2 and 4: inside the boundary it puts back the sum only, outside it puts back the ring and the dealt array too

@ a reset by an event at the frame 4, the frame of a tick, is after the tick: inside it keeps what the tick dealt, outside it puts back the two dealt elements, and the ring that is written from the frame 4 is whole for the tick 6
@ a when~ of an event inside the block reads the last event before the tick, at the run: all runs of a tick run or stop together
@ a when~ of an event outside the block reads the level at each frame and stops the block as a whole: its grid and its ring count the frames it runs
